items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: So he was only too glad for me to sit in for him. He'd go back behind and had a curtain, a long curtain. And I'd hear, you know, something he'd be squirting in his throat, you know, or in his nostrils. So I was glad to play too. And it was alright with Jo.

ctx.x: Well, as you grew on in years, did you hear any more music?

Oh yeah, I, in spite of me hearing this music, I used to say, the second line just like the rest of the kids. We used to try sometime way away from home, you know, out of the neighborhood. I remember I, I think it was about the 30th of May and some friends of mine and I, we, we came all the way down to French Bar Town and the boys got behind us and ran us all the way to the podgers and ramparts, you know. And so I always did love music. I used to do a lot of whistling. I still do. And so, but I didn't have no…
Where was he from? He's from New Orleans.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: I used to play so loud I guess that's why he spoke about my lungs so I was only too glad to sit down in Joe Oliver's band.

ctx.x: Yeah, read at my home. And you can imagine, I didn't give Roy a chance to turn it on unless I was asking him something. So Dutre, he was kind of sickly. And he would let me play for him. He'd go back to Curtain and some kind of medicine in hell, a blend in hell, something like asthma. I learned that he was, while in the Navy he was shutting the hole where the gunpowder was and that caused that. So he'd always say to me, he called me Pardner. He'd say Pardner if I had the good lungs that you have in the wind I…
They did cheat the musicians. Yes, yes, yes.
